newsitem.title: USA: Grossman's signs letter to get liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Grossman's signs letter to get liquidity.

text.p: Grossman's Inc said Friday it had signed a letter of intent with an affiliate of the company's largest shareholder to get the liquidity that it needed to keep operating.

The company, which announced last month that it was experiencing a severe liquidity shortage, said it had signed the letter with JELD-WEN Inc, agreeing to work towards a definitive agreement by February 14.
It also said its board of directors had elected David Ferrari as president and chief executive officer of the company.
Ferrari will replace Robert Swanson, who resigned as chief executive officer but remained chairman of the board, it said.
The company said the board had appointed Thomas Ford as chief operating officer following the resignation of Stanley Berman, who also stepped down as president.

Grossman's said JELD-WEN would likely provide it with short-term, interim financing in the form of a convertible note, secured by a subordinated collateral position in the company's owned real estate.
"Conversion of the note would result in JELD-WEN, (Inc) owning 50 percent of the company's outstanding stock," it said.
Under the terms of the letter of intent, the company said it and JELD-WEN would try to get trade creditors to accept discounted payments for past obligations in the form of 90-day notes and stock.
Suppliers who sell goods to the company on credit terms would also receive a security position in the company's owned real estate, it added.
"The letter contemplates that the arrangements with trade creditors may be most expeditiously effected through a future Chapter 11 filing," it said.

Grossman's operates 15 stores under the name Contractors' Warehouse in California, Indiana, Kentucky and Ohio, and 26 stores under the name Mr. 2nd's Bargain Outlet in Massachusetts, New York and Rhode Island.
